key_insight: The paper proposes a parameter-decoupled training strategy so one unified medical model can both reason over clinical images and generate precise segmentations without the two tasks interfering with each other.
clinical_relevance: This could help future medical AI systems explain their answers by pointing to the image regions they used, which may improve interpretability for clinicians.
method: Medical shallow alignment adapts visual features to clinical language while keeping the LLM largely stable.
Two-phase instruction tuning makes the <SEG> token act as a more separable semantic-to-spatial prompt, guided by DBI.
Segmentation gradients are scaled and the SAM branch is later specialized with the VLM frozen to improve masks without degrading reasoning.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on medical referring segmentation, grounding, visual QA, and textual QA benchmarks, with strong segmentation performance and competitive reasoning results.
watch_item: The approach adds training complexity and requires careful control of representation separation and gradient scaling to avoid unstable optimization or task trade-offs.
paper_title: SAM Meets VLM: Parameter-Decoupled Full-Parameter Training for Unified Medical Reasoning and Segmentation
